lawyer:
A.K.M. Nazrul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner

Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (ICB) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The Joint District Judge, First Court, Rangpur and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The writ-petitioner, the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh, filed Artha Rin Suit No. 85 of 2004 against respondent Nos. 2-6 for recovery of outstanding loan. Present respondent No. 2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank was defendant No. 5 in the Artha Rin Suit. The suit was ultimately decreed on contest against defendant Nos. 2, 4 and 5 and ex parte against the others by the judgment and order dated 09.10.2004. In the operative portion of that judgment, learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat made a direction that if defendant Nos. 2-4 would fail to pay the decreetal amount as per direction within the specified time the plaintiff-corporation could realize that amount by selling the mortgaged property. But in that case, the claimed amount of defendant No. 5, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, would be paid first from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged property. After satisfying the claim of defendant No. 5, the remaining sale proceeds would be adjusted against the decreetal amount by selling other immovable and moveable properties of judgment debtor-defendant Nos. 2-4. After a lapse of two years of that judgment, on 28.09.2006, the decree holder corporation filed an application under sections 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for correction of the operative portion of the judgment by deleting the direction given for satisfying the claim of defendant No. 5, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank first from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged property. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application holding that there was no scope for correction of the judgment and order passed earlier. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 12.03.2007 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Rangpur in Artha Rin Suit No. 85 of 2004 rejecting the writ-petitioner's application for correction of the operative portion of the judgment and order dated 09.10.2004, the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh as the writ-petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 1019 of 2009 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule Nisi. 

 8. Mr. A. K. M. Nazrul Islam, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the Leave petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the writ petition summarily in not at all pursuing the same as well as failed to appreciate the term of creating 'pari-passu' charge which gives the petitioner to hold self-same authority as that of Bangladesh Shilpa Bank over the mortgaged property and that since the writ-petitioner obtained the decree against respondent Nos. 3 to 6 there is no bar to realizing the decreetal amount so passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 85 of 2004 by selling the mortgaged property in pursuance of `pari-passu' charge. He further submits that the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the writ-petition summarily on the basis of admission of the learned Advocate for the writ-petitioner and but that mere holding first charge over the mortgaged property does not Ipso facto render the mortgagee to get its claim until and unless it is proved through adjudication by a competent Court. 

 9. We have considered the impugned judgment, the submissions of the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioner and the materials on record, admittedly the leave-petitioner, Investment Corporation of Bangladesh, filed Artha Rin Suit No. 85 of 2004 against respondent Nos. 2-6 for recovery of outstanding loan. Respondent No. 2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, was defendant No. 5 in that Artha Rin Suit which was ultimately decreed on contest against defendant Nos. 2, 4, and 5 and ex-parte against others by the judgment and decree dated 09.10.2004. In the operative portion of that judgment, the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat made a direction that if defendant Nos.  2-4 failed to pay the decreetal amount as per the direction within the specified time, the plaintiff-Corporation could realize the amount by selling the mortgaged property but that the amount claimed by defendant No. 5, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank would be paid first from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged property and that the remaining sale proceeds, if any, would be adjusted   against the decreetal amount of the leave-petitioner by selling other immoveable properties of the judgment-debtors, defendant Nos. 2-4. 

 10. After a lapse about two years of passing   of that judgment, the decree-holder filed an application under sections 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 28.09.2006 praying for correction of the operative portion of the judgment by deleting the direction for satisfying the claim of defendant No. 5, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank from the sale proceeds of the mortgaged property. The learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application on 12.03.2007 holding that there was no scope for correction of the judgment and order as prayed for under sections 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
